newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria eyes free trade accord with Poland by Jun.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria eyes free trade accord with Poland by Jun.

text.p: Bulgaria hopes to sign a free trade accord with Poland by mid-1997 in a bid to boost bilateral trade and help it in its move to join the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA), a senior official said on Thursday.

"We think the first round of talks to liberalise trade with Poland this week was very successful, which makes us optimistic that a free trade agreement could be reached by mid-year," Bulgaria's deputy trade minister Minko Gerdzhikov said.

The agreement with Poland is seen as an important step towards Bulgaria's membership in CEFTA and building closer economic ties with traditional trade partners such as Poland, he told a news conference.
Earlier this year, Bulgaria signed free trade agreements with the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia.

Under preliminary plans discussed this week, customs duties on certain Bulgarian and Polish goods should be lifted by 2000-2002, but details are yet to be agreed during the second round of talks at the end of April, Gerdzhikov said.

Bulgaria posted a gap of $2 million in trade with Poland last year with exports to Poland totalling $30 million and imports amounting to $32 million, he said. Comparative figures for 1995 were not available.
Bulgarian exports include mainly machinery and farm produce and bilateral trade has dropped significantly in recent years, Gerdzhikov said.

Bulgaria has to clear an oustanding debt to Poland worth of 110 million transferable rubles in January and the ministry hopes the debt will be repaid by Bulgarian exports by the end of the year, he said. @
Transferable rubles were used for payments between former comumunist block countries. Their exact equivalent in dollars is agreed upon on bilateral basis.
